problemStatement.formal:
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ such that\[\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1?\]



The Gaussian moat problem. This is not actually a problem of Erd\H{o}s, but has been erroneously attributed to him in the past. In \cite{Er77c} Erd\H{o}s recalls: 'The conjecture was told me by Motzkin at the Pasadena number theory meeting 1963 November and it was apparently raised by Basil Gordon and Motzkin. I naturally liked it very much and told it right away to many people, naturally attributing it to Motzkin, but this was later forgotten. Thus the problem is returned to its rightful owners.'

Key technique: z*star(z)=norm(z), so z|norm(z). By induction z|↑p for some rational prime p. Then norm(z)|p², giving norm=p or p²
For norm=p²: z~↑p (associated), so ↑p prime in ℤ[i], hence p≡3 mod 4 by GaussianInt.prime_iff_mod_four_eq_three_of_nat_prime

Proof skeleton: case-split on Prime z direction: (a) z.norm=2 → use natAbs_norm_eq + decide; (b) z.norm=p² with p≡3 mod 4 → derive z associates ↑p via Zsqrtd.norm_eq_mul_conj, then GaussianInt.prime_iff_mod_four_eq_three_of_nat_prime; (c) z.norm=p with p≡1 mod 4 → use Nat.Prime.sq_add_sq + irreducible_iff_prime in Euclidean domain.

Reverse direction (norm-classification ⇒ prime): each case uses Zsqrtd.norm_mul to verify minimality / no proper divisor. Norm 2 case: 1+i is the only norm-2 Gaussian integer up to units; computational. Norm p case: any factorization gives z=z₁z₂ with norm(z₁)·norm(z₂)=p, forcing one factor a unit.
